newsitem.title: UK: Best-selling UK paper switches from Major to Blair.
newsitem.headline: Best-selling UK paper switches from Major to Blair.

text.p: Britain's best-selling newspaper, the Sun, said on Monday that it was throwing its weight behind the main opposition Labour party in the coming election.
The Sun's decision will be a bitter blow to Prime Minister John Major, who enjoyed the tabloid's backing at the last election in 1992.
After Major confounded the opinion polls and won that election, the Sun crowed that it was "The Sun Wot Won It".
Under the headline "The Sun Backs Blair", the paper, owned by Australian-born media magnate Rupert Murdoch, will say in an editorial in Tuesday's edition: "This is the election for the millennium.
"In six weeks' time, Britain will vote for a government to take it into the 21st Century.
"The people need a leader with vision, purpose and courage who can inspire them and fire their imaginations.
"The Sun believes that man is Tony Blair," the paper, which sells more than four million copies a day, said.
It said Blair, hot favourite in opinion polls to succeed Major after the May 1 election, would be the best man for its readers and for Britain.
"It is a momentous decision which we have not taken lightly because we still have reservations about some of New Labour's policies.

"But for all the Tories' achievements of the past 18 years, they no longer deserve our support. They are tired, divided and rudderless. They need a rest and so does the country. Blair is the breath of fresh air this great country needs," it said.
Blair raised eyebrows last year when he accepted an invitation by Murdoch to address senior executives of his News Corp Ltd in Australia.

Prodded by Blair's press secretary, Alistair Campbell, himself a former tabloid journalist with the Labour-supporting Daily Mirror, Labour has worked hard to at least neutralise popular newspapers such as The Sun that backed Major in 1992.

Blair has periodically been given space in the Sun's columns to air his views. His most recent article appeared in Monday's newspaper. In it he promised voters that Labour would oppose the emergence of a federal European superstate.
